content: Doubt thou the stars are fire; Doubt that the sun doth move; Doubt truth to be a liar; But never doubt I love.
author: William Shakespeare
story:
Surviving devastating outbreaks of bubonic plague in Elizabethan and Jacobean London that repeatedly shuttered the Globe Theatre, Shakespeare channeled the entire spectrum of human passion, betrayal, ambition, and mortality onto the stage, creating portraits of the human condition that remain unparalleled across literary history.

Exploring the mysteries of human connection, William Shakespeare saw that genuine fulfillment cannot be hoarded or manufactured through egoic control. It blossoms only when we lower our defenses, dissolve self-importance, and meet the world with openhearted generosity.
reflectionPrompt: How can you extend greater compassion to yourself for your own imperfections right now?
